## 1. Background

A knowledge backup on Kendall's W test to support the test of majority vote. 

### 1A Majority voting criteria

```{r}
library(knitr)

criteria <- data.frame(
  Criterion = c("C1", "C2", "C3", "C4"),
  Definition = c(
    "≥1/4 raters positive", # at least 1/4 raters positive
    "≥2/4 raters positive",
    "≥3/4 raters positive",
    "4/4 raters positive"# All four raters positive
  )
)

kable(criteria, caption = "Positivity Criteria")
```

```{r}
# Dummy data
# Based on majority vote, incidence of lesion decrease
# As the criteria go more stringent
lesion_data <- data.frame(
  Lesion = c("Telangiectasia", "Superficial wrinkles", "Deep wrinkles", "Yellow papules"),
  `≥1/4` = c("80%", "75%", "65%", "40%"),
  `≥2/4` = c("70%", "65%", "55%", "30%"),
  `≥3/4` = c("60%", "55%", "45%", "20%"),
  `4/4` = c("45%", "40%", "35%", "10%"),
  check.names = FALSE
)

kable(lesion_data, caption = "Lesion Positivity Rates by Criterion")
```

```{r}
# A data frame of the ranking of lesions
# Under different majority voting criteria
lesion_data <- data.frame(
  Lesion = c("Telangiectasia", "Superficial wrinkles", "Deep wrinkles", "Yellow papules"),
  `≥1/4` = c(1, 2, 3, 4),
  `≥2/4` = c(1, 2, 3, 4),
  `≥3/4` = c(1, 2, 3, 4),
  `4/4` = c(1, 2, 3, 4),
  check.names = FALSE
)

kable(lesion_data, caption = "Lesion Scores by Criterion")
```

## 2. Implement Kendall's W manually

### 2A. Original ranking data

```{r}

rank_data2 <- rank_data2 |>
  mutate(rank_sum = loose + moderate + stringent + strictest)
```

$n = 4$ subjects (lesions)

$m = 4$ raters (positivity criteria)

### 2B. Calculate the rank sums

Mean rank sum

$$
\bar{R} = \frac{m(n + 1)}{2}
$$

Each rater assigns ranks $1 \dots n$, which sum to $n(n = 1)/2$

Across $m$ raters the total is $mn(n + 1)/2$, dividing by $n$ items

gives the mean rank $m(n + 1)/2$

### 2C. Calculate S

$$
S = \sum_{j = 1}^{n}(R_j - \bar{R})^2
$$

### 2D. Calculate Kendall's W

$$
W = \frac{12S}{m^2(n^3 - 1)}
$$

### 2E. Calculate the chi-square

$$
\chi^2 = m(n -1)W
$$

$df = n - 1$

## 3. Implement in irr package

### 3A-Scenario 1 perfect concordance case.

```{r}
rank_data <- data.frame(
  loose     = c(1, 2, 3, 4),
  moderate  = c(1, 2, 3, 4),
  stringent = c(1, 2, 3, 4),
  strictest = c(1, 2, 3, 4)
)

kendall(rank_data, correct = TRUE)
```

### 3B-Scenario 2 not in concordance

```{r}
irr::kendall(rank_data2[, c("loose", "moderate", "stringent", "strictest")],
  correct = TRUE
)
```
